title: Deuteronomy Bible Quiz - Chapter 16
description: Ten questions on Deuteronomy 16: the Passover, the feasts of weeks and booths, and fair judges.

questions.text: In which month were the Israelites told to keep the Passover?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says to observe the month of Abib and keep the Passover, because in that month Yahweh brought them out of Egypt by night.

answers.text: The month of Adar
The month of Ziv
The month of Elul
The month of Abib

questions.text: What does verse 3 call the unleavened bread eaten with the Passover?
questions.explanation: They were to eat unleavened bread seven days, "the bread of affliction", because they came out of Egypt in haste.

answers.text: The bread of heaven
The bread of the presence
The bread of affliction
The bread of peace

questions.text: Where were the Israelites allowed to sacrifice the Passover?
questions.explanation: They could not sacrifice it within any of their gates, but only at the place Yahweh would choose to cause his name to dwell.

answers.text: At the place Yahweh would choose for his name
In any town of the land they were given
In each family's own house, at the door
At the border of the land, near the Jordan

questions.text: How was the Passover to be prepared before it was eaten?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says: "You shall roast and eat it in the place which Yahweh your God chooses."

answers.text: It was boiled in water
It was eaten raw
It was dried in the sun
It was roasted

questions.text: From when were the seven weeks before the feast of weeks to be counted?
questions.explanation: They were to begin counting seven weeks from the time they first put the sickle to the standing grain.

answers.text: From the first new moon of the new year
From when the sickle was first put to the standing grain
From the last day of the grape harvest
From the day the Passover lamb was chosen

questions.text: When was the feast of booths to be kept?
questions.explanation: Verse 13 says to keep the feast of booths seven days after gathering in from the threshing floor and the wine press.

answers.text: After gathering in from the threshing floor and wine press
Before the first seed was sown in the fields
When the first lambs of the flock were born
On the day the sickle was first put to the grain

questions.text: At which three feasts did all the males have to appear before Yahweh?
questions.explanation: Three times a year all males were to appear before Yahweh: at the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of weeks and the feast of booths.

answers.text: Unleavened bread, trumpets and new moons
Unleavened bread, weeks and booths
Weeks, booths and the feast of the king
Passover, harvest and the Sabbath year

questions.text: How was every man to give when he appeared before Yahweh?
questions.explanation: They were not to appear empty; every man was to give as he was able, according to the blessing Yahweh had given him.

answers.text: As he was able, according to Yahweh's blessing
Exactly one tenth of his flock
A half shekel, the same for everyone
Only what the priest demanded

questions.text: According to verse 19, what does a bribe do?
questions.explanation: Verse 19 forbids taking a bribe, "for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous."

answers.text: It makes the poor rich
It blinds the eyes of the wise
It shortens the life of the judge
It brings rain on the wicked

questions.text: What were the Israelites told not to plant beside Yahweh's altar?
questions.explanation: Verse 21 says they must not plant an Asherah of any kind of tree beside Yahweh their God's altar.

answers.text: A vineyard of choice vines
A field of barley or wheat
An Asherah of any kind of tree
A row of olive trees
